title: Thieves are swiping Bigfoot signs around Carrollton
excerpt: Bigfoot silhouette signs are mysteriously missing in Carroll County. Organizers of Charity event at St. John's Villa are disappointed.
content:
Oct. 9, 2026, 5:31 a.m. ET

CARROLLTON ‒ Kimberly Lewis tried to keep the tone light when she first announced that signs advertising a Sasquatch-themed event were disappearing.

In a Sept. 23 post on Facebook, she asked the public to help find a Bigfoot belonging to St. John's Villa that went missing from a property on state Route 43 south of state Route 171.

"We believe he had help," wrote Lewis, co-director of marketing and communications for St. John's. "If you see him, please return him to the farm or to St. John's Villa. When a (Bigfoot) is removed from his habitat, he is very, very scared. We are concerned for his mental health."

The signs, shaped like silhouettes of the cryptid, announce the second annual Carroll County Squatch Fest & Parapalooza, to be held from noon to 5 p.m. Oct. 17 at St. John's, 701 Crest St. NW. The event will feature speakers, a marketplace, a kids' zone and food trucks. The event is free with a donation requested for parking.

About a dozen of the signs were placed in and around Carrollton to promote the event being held by St. John's Villa, a nonprofit organization that provides residential and day services for individuals with developmental and intellectual disabilities. It also operates a child care center and a restaurant.

Loss value estimated at more than $500

So far, five of the signs have been swiped. Lewis said the largest was nearly 8 feet tall. A truck would have been needed to take it away. The others were about 4 feet tall. When a police report was made about the first four thefts, the value of the signs was estimated at $500. They were crafted by staff at the facility.

Lewis said the thefts began on the weekend of Sept. 19 and 20. The most recent disappearance was on Oct. 6.

"It has been brought to our attention that another one of our signs have been stolen from Lisbon Street," St. John's Director Susan Williamson wrote Oct. 7 on Facebook. "I don't understand why someone would think that it is ok to trespass onto someone's property and steal from their yard. This was supposed to be a fun way for us to advertise and grow our event.

"I know someone knows who is responsible for stealing our signs. We would greatly appreciate any information in regard to the theft of the signs so that they can be returned," Williamson wrote.

Kimberly Lewis: 'We’re hoping that they get returned'

Lewis says St. John’s Villa hosts community events to help raise funds for developmentally disabled adults.

“I think for us it's very frustrating because you want to do this event for the public and you want to make it fun for everyone," Lewis said by phone on Oct. 8. "And you worked really hard on advertising and then to have your signs just disappear, I think is very disappointing. We thought it would be clever and we thought it'd really catch everybody's attention. And it did ... not the way we expected. ” 

She tried to keep a sense of humor about the missing figures.

"I think they're developing their own tribe," Lewis said. "People have called us with sightings, you know, the silhouettes, not the live one. We’re hoping that they get returned.”

St. John's is selling the Sasquatch silhouettes. The larger ones cost $150, and the smaller ones, $50. They may be ordered at the Oct. 17 event.

Anyone with information about the missing signs is asked to call Lewis or Williamson at 330-627-9789, or the Carrollton Police Department at 330-627-2858.
